need to think about how this will interact with any special handling we do of whitespace-only caBundle fields
@liggitt what special handling do you have in mind?

given there are a *lot* of CRDs with invalid caBundles scattered around the internet (https://grep.app/search?q=otherwise%20it%20will%20be%20rejected%20by%20the%20apiserver%20for%20being%20blank&regexp=true&filter[lang][0]=YAML) with whitespace-only caBundle fields, it's clear many things expect a workflow where a CRD is created with a whitespace-only caBundle which is then updated asynchronously.

I'm wondering how we can best handle the following scenarios:

1. new CRDs that show up with placeholder caBundle values and expect to get updated by something like cert-manager to make them valid to serve
2. existing CRDs with placeholder caBundle values are not getting updated by something like cert-manager and are failing to serve and disrupting discovery clients / namespace controller
3. updates can make a valid caBundle value invalid, breaking serving on an existing CRD


I think I'd suggest the following:
1. For CRDs that do not have an Established=True condition (on CRD creation or pre-serving updates)
   * In validation, allow arbitrary caBundle values like today
   * In staging/src/k8s.io/apiextensions-apiserver/pkg/controller/establish/establishing_controller.go, gate setting Established=True on the caBundle value being valid (if specified). This means until caBundle is populated with a valid value in a new CRD, the CRD will not be served and will not show up in discovery.
2. For CRDs that *do* have an Established=True condition (which means they are being served)
   * In validation, add ratcheting validation (this PR) so valid caBundle values have to stay valid
   * When constructing the webhook conversion client in webhookClientConfigForCRD, *consider* special-casing whitespace-only values to treat them as an empty value and fall back to system trust roots. This will still likely fail when attempting to contact the conversion webhook, but reads/writes that don't require conversion could still succeed, so if there were no persisted objects or only requests to the version matching the storage version and all existing persisted objects were in that version, clients like the namespace controller could be unblocked.

Given that there are a lot of existing offending CRDs: maybe we could *also* submit https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/123827 ? This will both provide motivation for CRD owners to upgrade, while lowering the impact on apiserver (currently, it can lead to eg. blocked namespace deletion)

> I think I'd suggest the following:
> 
> 1. For CRDs that do not have an Established=True condition (on CRD creation or pre-serving updates)
>    
>    * In validation, allow arbitrary caBundle values like today
>    * In staging/src/k8s.io/apiextensions-apiserver/pkg/controller/establish/establishing_controller.go, gate setting Established=True on the caBundle value being valid (if specified). This means until caBundle is populated with a valid value in a new CRD, the CRD will not be served and will not show up in discovery.

I wonder if we could provide more incentive for users to "upgrade" and fix sending invalid caBundles. I agree that breaking clients is not an ideal workflow, but maybe we can provide some kind of warning when CRDs are created with invalid caBundles to encourage users to fix their inputs?

> 2. For CRDs that _do_ have an Established=True condition (which means they are being served)
>    
>    * In validation, add ratcheting validation (this PR) so valid caBundle values have to stay valid

+1, will update this PR.

>    * When constructing the webhook conversion client in webhookClientConfigForCRD, _consider_ special-casing whitespace-only values to treat them as an empty value and fall back to system trust roots. This will still likely fail when attempting to contact the conversion webhook, but reads/writes that don't require conversion could still succeed, so if there were no persisted objects or only requests to the version matching the storage version and all existing persisted objects were in that version, clients like the namespace controller could be unblocked.

This basically a variation https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/123827 right?

> I wonder if we could provide more incentive for users to "upgrade" and fix sending invalid caBundles. I agree that breaking clients is not an ideal workflow, but maybe we can provide some kind of warning when CRDs are created with invalid caBundles to encourage users to fix their inputs?

Yeah, a warning would be helpful, actually, telling them the CRD won't be served until the invalid CA bundle is fixed.

> Given that there are a lot of existing offending CRDs: maybe we could also submit https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/123827 ? This will both provide motivation for CRD owners to upgrade, while lowering the impact on apiserver (currently, it can lead to eg. blocked namespace deletion)

I'd special-case the whitespace-only bundles, and only in conjunction with keeping *new* CRDs from being established.

> This basically a variation https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/123827 right?

Yeah, but I would make it proactive (dropping whitespace-only caBundle at construction time) instead of reactive (detecting an error after client construction)

issue_context.title: CRD validation allows invalid CABundles that will fail setting up handlers
issue_context.body:
### What happened?

A CRDs with an invalid conversion webhook CABundle failed to serve requests not requiring conversion.


### What did you expect to happen?

Since creating cr-1.yaml doesn't require conversion, I would have expected either:

1. An error response when attempting to create/update the CRD with an invalid CABundle
2. Only an error when conversion is required to server a request

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?


Create a mult-version CRD with a conversion webhook configured with an invalid CABundle:

```yaml
apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1
kind: CustomResourceDefinition
metadata:
  name: replicant.stable.example.com
spec:
  group: stable.example.com
  versions:
    - name: v1
      served: true
      storage: true
      schema:
        openAPIV3Schema:
          type: object
          properties:
            spec:
              type: object
              properties:
                myfield:
                  type: integer
    - name: v2
      served: true
      storage: false
      schema:
        openAPIV3Schema:
          type: object
          properties:
            spec:
              type: object
              properties:
                myfield:
                  type: integer
  scope: Namespaced
  names:
    plural: replicant
    singular: replicants
    kind: Replicant
  conversion:
    strategy: Webhook
    webhook:
      conversionReviewVersions: [v1]
      clientConfig:
        service:
          namespace: default
          name: example-conversion-webhook-server
          path: /convert
        caBundle: "Cg=="
```

```
$ kubectl apply -f crd.yaml
customresourcedefinition.apiextensions.k8s.io/replicant.stable.example.com created
```

Read the CRD back:

```
$ kubectl get crd replicant.stable.example.com -oyaml
apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1
kind: CustomResourceDefinition
...
```

Attempt to create a CR using the storage version:

```yaml
apiVersion: stable.example.com/v1
kind: Replicant
metadata:
  name: cr1
spec:
  myfield: 1
```

```
$ kubectl apply cr1.yaml
Error from server (InternalError): error when retrieving current configuration of:
Resource: "stable.example.com/v1, Resource=replicant", GroupVersionKind: "stable.example.com/v1, Kind=Replicant"
Name: "cr1", Namespace: "default"
from server for: "cr-1.yaml": Internal error occurred: error resolving resource

$ grep "customresource_handler" /tmp/local-kube-apiserver.log
E0308 12:57:41.892888 1158130 customresource_handler.go:301] unable to load root certificates: unable to parse bytes as PEM block

```

> An error response when attempting to create/update the CRD with an invalid CABundle

I would have expected this... are we not parsing the CA bundle in CRD validation? We should do this in a ratcheting way

> > An error response when attempting to create/update the CRD with an invalid CABundle
>

> 
> I would have expected this... are we not parsing the CA bundle in CRD validation? We should do this in a ratcheting way

We are not. I'm okay with ratcheting validation.
Updated description to clarify the bug is that CRD validation permits the invalid CA bundle in the first place

Interesting, I think this is caused by something like https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kubebuilder/blob/011383cb93b1d26de2f421418fce26ea4bd66700/pkg/plugins/golang/v2/scaffolds/internal/templates/config/crd/patches/enablewebhook_patch.go#L55-L57

That workaround is not required in 1.13+ clusters (the apiserver doesn't reject webhooks with empty caBundle fields), but is still present in old kubebuilder versions and lots of CRD manifests in the wild, so any user installing kubebuilder-created CRDs with conversion webhooks whose CA Bundle update mechanism is not working will encounter this error.

The kube-builder repo removed the workaround years ago in https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kubebuilder/pull/1699, but it looks like lots of CRD manifests in the wild have the single-newline placeholder for caBundle:

[https://grep.app/search?q=caBundle%3A%20cg%3D%3D&filter[lang][0]=YAML](https://grep.app/search?q=caBundle%3A%20cg%3D%3D&filter%5Blang%5D%5B0%5D=YAML)

review_comments: this is worth a comment explaining why we allow it to be invalid on create (since it's not yet established)

in the controller where we set Established=true (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/apiextensions-apiserver/pkg/controller/establish/establishing_controller.go#L119), after names are accepted, we now need to check if the caBundle is valid before setting Established=True

if it is not, set Established=False with a specific reason indicating the caBundle is not valid

add a unit test that ensures:
* empty is valid
* non-empty with a valid cert is valid
* non-empty without any certs is invalid
* non-empty with malformed certs is invalid

Added. The case for "non-empty without any certs is invalid" and "non-empty with malformed certs is invalid" is handled in the same way when validating via creating the transport, but added test cases for both.
